what_was_done: (a) Out-degree 0 in the degree-normalised ranking (SPEC 8.1, addendum 3 A.1). This case only arises in metapath mode. When a node has no arc under the configured direction, its out-degree is now the number of reach-DAG arcs leaving it, counting each (u, v, kind, orientation) once. Before this fix, the reference arm divided by zero and got infinity, and the relational arm silently dropped the term (SQLite returns NULL for division by zero).

(a) New self-test, arms/common/selftest.js section 12: a 7-node metapath graph with the scores worked out by hand in a comment. Nodes a, b, c, d, e, f, x get ids 1 to 7; the edges are a->b, a->c, c->f, d->b, e->b, x->b and x->c, all calls. The direction is dependencies and the steps are 'calls out' then 'calls in'. Node b has out-degree 0, so its 3 DAG arcs are used instead. Expected scores: x 2/3, b 1/2, c 1/2, d 1/6, e 1/6. Both arms return exactly these, byte-identical, and also inside a hybrid ranking.

(b) A metapath step whose edge kinds are all absent at a commit reaches nothing in both arms, without error. The relational arm builds its step table from the (kind, class) pairs present at the commit; the reference arm matches kinds by name. Self-test section 13 covers three cases: a step of the absent kind enqueues_kind (only the hop-1 nodes with emit all, nothing with emit end), and a single step of an absent class (nothing). The focused random cross-check also covered 147 such pairs.

(c) Answer record, built in arms/common/harness.js: `meta` from rank() is now carried into each answer, with any `ledger` array replaced by `ledger_len`. For search this gives tokens_read, r1_lookups, names, routes, ledger_len and seed_in_tree.

(c) Lookups are now counted in one place (PAD_LOOKUPS in harness.js). New fields: lookups_head (the arm's own count; 1 when the arm reports nothing; 0 for an empty head), lookups_pad (DIR 1, CO 2, none 0, the same for every arm) and lookups = lookups_head + lookups_pad. The floor arms and the built-in arm 'none' now report 0 for their head.

ladybugFix.status: Done. All the addendum 3 fixes (sections A, B and C) are in the LadybugDB arm. what_was_done: a. Degree-normalised ranking (lb.js scoreFor 'degnorm'). When a node that the reach graph leaves from has out-degree 0 under the configured direction, classes and minConf, its out-degree is now the number of reach-DAG arcs leaving it, each (u, v, kind, orientation) counted once (SPEC 8.1). The old code divided by zero. This also covers the typed-path-pattern metapath variant.

b. Community prior (store.js commPrior and nativePriors). The Louvain grouping is now stored once per canonical graph in arms/ladybug/priors/<canonical content hash>.json, with labels renumbered by first appearance. The first build of a graph writes the file with an atomic hard link, so it is never overwritten and two processes racing on the same graph end up with the same grouping. Every later build reads the file into N.comm and records how its own Louvain run compares with it. The switch LB_COMM_DRAW=k (1 to 4) selects priors/<hash>.draw<k>.json and a separate store, because the store key includes the draw. If that file is missing, the build draws it with the same louvain() on the same code graph, in a scratch database loaded in a seeded random row order (seed 20261112 + 7919 k). This makes each draw fresh and reproducible. Store version bumped from LB5 to LB6.

c. x_prank: page_rank now runs on a projection (PR_FILTER) that holds both orientations of every co_changed edge. A toy probe (tmp/ladybug/probe_pr.js) showed how LadybugDB's page_rank behaves: it is directed, teleports uniformly with damping 0.85, and drops the mass of dangling nodes, so the scores sum to less than 1. Its scores are proportional to the textbook version that spreads dangling mass uniformly (a constant ratio of 2.5525 on every node of the toy), so the order of candidates is the same. This is written in NOTES.md.

d. x_wsp: the cost of an edge is its kind's cost divided by max(confidence, 0.05). A hub-blocked node can end a path but is never passed through: the hub predicate is in the recursive WSHORTEST filter, and each blocked candidate gets min over its unblocked predecessors u of cost(u) + cost(u, v). The kind-cost table is written in NOTES.md for the DuckPGQ lane.

NOTES.md and the bench output (latency._note) now say that the default PageRank runs its iterations in application code over a transition adjacency cached in application code. bench.js now reports first_call (the first answer with no cache) and warm_uncached (repeated calls with the application caches dropped before each), beside cold and warm.

duckpgqFix.status: Done. All six fixes from addendum 3 (items a to f) are in the DuckPGQ arm, which runs on DuckDB 2.0.0 with DuckPGQ extension 9c11bc192a. what_was_done: Fix a (degree-normalised ranking): when a node has no arc in the configured direction, its out-degree is now the number of distinct reach-DAG arcs leaving it, as SPEC 8.1 says. Before, such a node dropped out of the activation join.

Fix b (k-hop): a bounded k-hop no longer computes path lengths beyond the hop limit. The default form is a recursive SQL statement keyed on the node that stops expanding at depth H. A second form ('levels') uses one one-edge PGQ pattern per level, starting from the current frontier. DuckPGQ has no bounded shortest-path routine: iterativelength() always runs to the end of the graph. That is why iterativelength() is now used only for unbounded k-hop.

Fix c (metapath): a metapath step whose kinds are all absent now matches no arc (its predicate is FALSE). Walk patterns that would pass through that step are dropped, so the SQL 'AND ()' error is gone.

Fix d (graph built once): two property graphs are now stored inside each store file at build time: g (vertex table node, edge table arc) and gtq (the TQ labels). The store is opened READ_ONLY as the main database. ATTACH could not be kept: a probe (probe/probe10.js) showed that a stored graph is not visible through ATTACH, and a read-only database cannot create a graph. A configuration's projection is no longer a table or a graph; it is an edge-element filter on the stored arc label, or the filtered row source of a CSR. Nothing is declared per connection. DuckDB now uses 6 threads, which is os.availableParallelism() in the container (it was 4). The build time of the connection caches (hub sets, PPR transitions, native results) still counts inside engine time, the same as in the relational arm, and is also reported on its own in meta.setup_ms.

Fix e (x_wsp): the LadybugDB definition is adopted. Arc cost = class cost / max(confidence, 0.05). The class costs are copied from arms/ladybug/store.js CLASS_COST: structure, imports, calls, http and tests 1; data and config 1.5; history 2; capability, docs and experimental 3; membership 4; any other class 3. A hub-blocked node keeps no out-arc, so no path passes through it (seeds exempt). Score = 1 / (1 + the minimum cost from any seed). The stage-1 entries 'x_wsp' and 'hybrid ppr+x_wsp' now have the same configuration hashes as LadybugDB's entries. A variant with kind costs B is kept as an extra native entry.

New mode x_wsp (arm extension). It is registered in arms/relational/rel.js (EXT_RANK.x_wsp) and the SQL is in arms/relational/queries.js (wsp_init, wsp_relax, wsp_score; temp tables wd and wcost). The definition follows LadybugDB, addendum 3 A.2: arc cost = class cost / max(confidence, 0.05), with the class costs copied from the LadybugDB store. Arcs follow the configuration's direction, classes and minConf. A hub-blocked node may end a path but is never expanded. Path length is unbounded. Score = 1/(1+min cost), ordered score desc, hop asc, id asc. It runs as set-based Bellman-Ford in rounds: one upsert relaxation statement per round, driven by a thin loop until a round changes nothing. The written definition is in arms/relational/NOTES.md.

Added two new modes from the catalogue in the new file arms/search/fuse.js; search.js and engine.js were edited to use them. Mode `co` (true or false) is a co-change part: the output of `git log` for the seed file, over the ancestor commits in commits.jsonl. It uses the same commit-counting rule and order as the shared CO tail (count, then recency, then path), keeps only code, test and migration files that exist at the parent, and costs one lookup whose tokens are the 'count path' lines. It reads commits, not facts edges. Mode `fuse` ('sum' or 'rrf') is how the file rankings are combined: 'sum' is the stage-1 sum of max-normalised scores, 'rrf' is reciprocal-rank fusion with k = 60. Both fields are optional; when absent the behaviour is stage 1, so stage-1 hashes and answers are unchanged.

Rankings did differ where the budget binds: recall at 2,000 tokens ranged from 0.465 to 0.500, and the PPR+text hybrid had the best top-10 file share (0.550). The plan was therefore to cross reach (3 hops, 4 hops, unbounded) with ranking, padding, hub cuts and granularity.

The 20, with complexity (cx) and one-line reasons. (1) s2: hops=3 + pad=CO, cx 2: the simplest way to reach the unbounded level; 3 hops already fill the budget on most tasks and the CO tail covers the rest. (2) s2: hops=4 + pad=CO, cx 3: the same interaction one hop further. (3) s2: hops=null + pad=CO, cx 3: the best reach plus a tail for seeds in small components (on T1x, CO padding scored 0.603 against 0.592 for unbounded hops). (4) s2: hops=3 + rank=degnorm, cx 1: at 3 hops the order decides the cut, and degnorm had the best recall at 2,000 tokens (0.499 against 0.478). (5) s2: hops=3 + rank=cochange, cx 1: co-changed files first; high top-10 share (0.527) and the cheapest ranking. (6) s2: hops=3 + rank=ppr r0.50, cx 1: a more local PageRank for a larger reach (0.491 against 0.478 at 2,000 tokens).

(7) s2: hops=3 + rank=hybrid ppr+text, cx 2: had the best top-10 share (0.550) and nDCG@10 (0.476); tested where order binds. (8) s2: hops=3 + rank=cochange + pad=CO, cx 2: history in both places, co-change order inside the reach and the co-change tail after it. (9) s2: hops=null + rank=bfs, cx 2: does closest-first order suffice when the reach is the whole component? (10) s2: hops=null + rank=degnorm, cx 2: the best early-recall ranking on the best reach. (11) s2: hops=null + rank=cochange, cx 2: every co-changed file is one hop away, so this is the CO floor order followed by graph order by hop. (12) s2: hops=null + rank=ppr r0.50, cx 2: keeps PageRank mass near the seeds when the reach is about 1,660 nodes.

(13) s2: hops=null + rank=hybrid ppr+cochange, cx 3: fuses the two strongest single signals. (14) s2: hops=null + rank=hybrid ppr+text, cx 3: the best top-10 ranking on the best reach. (15) s2: hops=null + hub=transport, cx 3: with surplus reach a hub cut can no longer starve the answer. (16) s2: hops=null + hub=indeg>10, cx 3: hop limit with hub cut; this cut lost reach at 2 hops but may focus PageRank at unbounded reach. (17) s2: hops=null + hub=indeg>15, cx 3: a milder cut, so the hub curve has two points. (18) s2: hops=null + gran=symbol, cx 3: symbol granularity was reach-starved at 2 hops (2,651 tokens used). Layers. Unbounded k-hop runs through the property-graph (PGQ) layer: DuckPGQ's native iterativelength() function over a CSR (compressed adjacency table) of the projected arcs.
